stem: Gauri's class decides what counts as matter. They consider air in a balloon, a pebble, and a beam of torch light in a dark room. Matter must occupy space and have mass.

parts.text: Which claim correctly decides what is matter?

options.text: Air in the balloon is matter, because it occupies space and has mass.
Air in the balloon is not matter, because it cannot be seen.
The torch beam is matter, because it spreads across the dark room.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Matter must occupy space and have mass; air meets both, while a light beam spreading through space does not show mass, and invisibility is not the test.

teacher.key_rationale: Air occupies space and has mass, so it is matter. Visibility is not the criterion. Occupying space alone (as a light beam appears to) is not enough without mass.
